description:
FILED s536f (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while fixing #4341 (scratch/s536f/p/m1i.pl row 3 in the s536f worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: main c8886b61 answers the same.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    sub c { scalar(@_) . ":" . join(",", @_) }
    my $o = bless {a => 1}, 'X';
    print c(%$o), "\n";

perl: `2:a,1`.   PCL: `1:HASH(0x1)`.

WHY (read, not fixed): `%p-flatten-arg-into` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the per-argument rule of p-flatten-args and p-map-flat) spreads a hash table only when it has no :__class__ key -- "NOT blessed objects (which have :__class__) -- those stay as-is".  But `%$o` hands the walker the REFERENT table (blessing lives in the table as :__class__), so the dereferenced hash of an object is passed whole; a reference to an object arrives as a BOX, never as a raw table, so the exclusion protects nothing that is still emitted (to be measured).  s536f factored the spreading into `%p-flatten-hash-into`, which already skips the :__class__ key, so the fix is the predicate (`(hash-table-p arg)` alone) -- measure first which callers hand a raw blessed table on purpose (grep `:__class__` around p-flatten-args / p-map-flat; the list-slice walk spreads it already).
BAR: the reproducer + `map { ... } %$o` + `push @l, %$o` as guard rows.


=== DONE (s536i) ===
a raw hash table in a LIST position spreads its pairs whether or not it carries the blessing key -- an object travels as its reference BOX, which never spreads: the exclusion is gone in %p-flatten-arg-into (p-flatten-args / p-map-flat), %p-args-need-flatten, the copying parameter flattener (which now skips :__class__), and push's two arms; p-unshift, which spread no hash at all, spreads one.  Probed: c(%$o), c(@$ao), my @l = (%$o), for (%$o), push / unshift, return %$x, map { %$_ }, a copying-params sub, a method, a coderef, a `%{}` overload -- all = perl.  Guard Pl/t/blessed-copy-01.t row 11 (fails on 3139fcb0).  Commit: subject `s536i WIP #4683`.
